sources.entry: bough by nickelsec - Reads Claude Code JSONL session transcripts and draws a project's history as a creatively-styled diagram: a day, the tasks inside it, and every prompt, with the ones that ended in a commit marked. Segments work from pauses in the record rather than anything the user labelled, and prompts can be searched by the words they contain.

summary.one_liner: A local tool that reads Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Pi session transcripts and draws a project's work as a diagram of sittings, tasks and prompts, with API-rate cost estimates.
summary.what_it_does: It reads JSONL/rollout session transcripts from Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Pi, and rebuilds three levels: prompts, tasks (runs of prompts toward one goal), and sittings (work sessions split by pauses). Tasks that ended in a git commit are marked, and the commit hash and message are shown; it reads the project's local git history to confirm commits. Each task and sitting carries a cost estimate in tokens and dollars at published API rates, built into the binary. It serves an interactive page on 127.0.0.1 and also offers a plain-text or JSON output mode, with prompts searchable by their words. Everything runs offline, and the tool only reads history and repositories.
use_cases: see what was built in a Claude Code project over time
estimate what AI coding sessions would have cost at API rates
find which prompt or task led to a given commit
review past Codex CLI or Pi sessions by project
export a project's session structure as JSON
trace work returning to the same files across sittings
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <script> | sh (Linux, or macOS without Homebrew)
bough (opens the project list in the browser)
stack: browser-based local page served on loopback
notable: Segments work into tasks and sittings from pauses, context compaction and subject/file changes rather than user labels
Links task cost to git commits, showing hash and message
Reads Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Pi transcripts; Pi providers priced individually, local models shown as (local)
Cost figures are at published API rates, not a bill; subscriptions are not reflected
Strictly read-only: no network, no writes to history or repositories
caveats: Thresholds are fitted to one developer's history and may not suit others; they are constants requiring code edits to change
Codex and Pi support is newer and less tested than Claude Code support
Struggle score is an unverified guess, off by default
Cost figures are estimates at API rates and do not reflect flat-rate subscriptions; models without published rates show NA
keywords: how much did ai coding cost
